title: Dialing in grind size
text: Adjust the grinder finer if the shot runs fast and sour. Coarser grind slows extraction and reduces bitterness in espresso.

title: Water temperature for brewing
text: Brew coffee between 92 and 96 celsius. Water that is too hot scalds the grounds and water that is too cool under extracts.

title: Removing mineral buildup
text: Hard water leaves limescale inside the brewer boiler and the brew unit. Flush the system monthly with a citric solution to dissolve the mineral buildup and restore flow.

title: Steam wand care
text: Purge the steam wand after every use and wipe it with a damp cloth so milk residue does not clog the tip.

title: Descaling guide
text: To descale the espresso machine, run the descale program with descaling solution. Descaling removes limescale and mineral buildup from the boiler.

title: Storing coffee beans
text: Keep beans in an airtight opaque container away from heat and light. Do not refrigerate beans because moisture ruins the aroma.

title: Error E-4417 water sensor
text: The display shows error code E-4417 when the machine stops. Reseat the water tank firmly and restart the machine to clear the error code.

title: Error E-4471 pump fault
text: The display shows error code E-4471 when the machine stops. Power cycle the pump unit and restart the machine to clear the error code.

title: Milk frothing basics
text: Stretch the milk with the wand tip near the surface, then submerge to spin a whirlpool until the jug is hot to the touch.

title: Portafilter cleaning
text: Soak the portafilter and basket in cleaning powder weekly. Coffee oils build up and turn shots rancid if the basket is dirty.

title: Choosing a burr grinder
text: Flat burrs give clarity while conical burrs give body. For espresso a stepless burr grinder allows fine adjustment.

title: Pre infusion explained
text: Pre infusion wets the puck at low pressure before full pressure, reducing channeling and evening out extraction.

title: Steep ridge climb
text: The ridge trail is steep and exposed, gaining 900 meters over rocky switchbacks. Only experienced hikers should attempt this steep route in wet weather.

title: Gentle valley loop
text: The valley loop is a flat easy walk beside the river, suitable for families. The gentle path has shade, benches, and no significant climbing.

title: Day hike packing list
text: Carry water, snacks, a rain shell, sunscreen, a map, and a headlamp. Pack layers because mountain weather changes quickly on a day hike.

title: Altitude sickness symptoms
text: Above 2500 meters watch for headache, nausea, dizziness, and poor sleep. Altitude sickness improves by descending and resting.

title: Leave no trace
text: Pack out all rubbish, stay on marked trails, and keep distance from wildlife so the trail stays wild for others.

title: Waterfall boardwalk
text: A short boardwalk leads to the waterfall viewpoint. The path is flat and wheelchair accessible with railings the whole way.

title: Trail running shoes
text: Trail shoes need aggressive lugs for grip on mud and a rock plate to protect the foot on technical ground.

title: River crossing safety
text: Unbuckle your pack, face upstream, and use poles. Never cross a river above knee depth after heavy rain.

title: Sunrise summit tips
text: Start hiking two hours before dawn with a headlamp. The summit is cold before sunrise so bring an insulated jacket.

title: Camping permits
text: Overnight camping in the reserve requires a permit booked online. Rangers check permits at the trailhead on weekends.

title: Blister prevention
text: Tape hot spots early, wear wool socks, and lace the heel lock. Wet skin blisters faster so change socks at lunch.

title: Navigation basics
text: Orient the map to north with a compass and tick off features as you pass. GPS batteries die, paper does not.

title: What is overfitting
text: Overfitting is when a model memorizes training data and fails on new data. The training loss keeps falling while validation loss rises.

title: Precision versus recall
text: Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are correct. Recall is the fraction of true positives that are found. Raising one usually lowers the other.

title: Learning rate too high
text: If the learning rate is too high the loss oscillates or diverges. Warmup and decay schedules keep optimization stable.

title: Regularization overview
text: Weight decay, dropout, and early stopping all limit model capacity to reduce overfitting and improve generalization.

title: Train test split
text: Hold out a test set that is never used for tuning. Leakage between splits inflates reported accuracy.

title: Batch size effects
text: Large batches give smoother gradients but may generalize worse. Small batches add noise that can act as regularization.

title: Cross validation
text: K fold cross validation rotates the held out fold so every example is tested once, giving a better estimate on small datasets.

title: Class imbalance
text: With rare positives, accuracy is misleading. Use precision, recall, and resampling or class weights instead.

title: Feature scaling
text: Standardize features to zero mean and unit variance so gradient descent converges faster and distances are comparable.

title: Confusion matrix
text: A confusion matrix counts true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives for a classifier.

title: Early stopping
text: Stop training when validation loss stops improving for several epochs and keep the best checkpoint.

title: Gradient clipping
text: Clip the gradient norm to a threshold to prevent exploding gradients in recurrent networks and transformers.
